summary: Recent updates to the Web Audio platform in Firefox have improved how the browser handles audio interruptions and optimizes audio playback. One significant change is the ability to **defer a page's request to resume audio after an interruption**, ensuring a smoother user experience when switching between tabs or applications. Additionally, the handling of `AudioContext`, which is crucial for scripting audio processing and playback, is now more robust, waiting for it to start properly before performing actions. Lastly, enhancements to buffer sizing during decoding help improve the efficiency and quality of audio playback. These changes collectively contribute to a more seamless experience for users engaging with audio content online.
